headline: Revenue grows, but rising costs squeeze margins and profit
summary_short: FactSet's fiscal Q3 (labeled FY2026 Q2 on this shard) revenue rose 6.4% y/y to $622.9M, but net income fell 14.7% to $126.7M and diluted EPS fell 9.6% to $3.50 as operating margin compressed to 26.7% from 33.2% a year ago.
summary_long: Revenue rose 6.4% y/y to $622.9M (7.0% organic growth, partly offset by a prior-year business disposition), with all three segments growing, led by the Americas from workstations and data solutions. Operating margin fell to 26.7% from 33.2% a year ago as cost of services rose 220bp and SG&A rose 430bp of revenue, driven by higher employee compensation, one-time CEO make-whole pay, and restructuring/severance charges. Net income fell 14.7% to $126.7M and diluted EPS fell 9.6% to $3.50, cushioned by 2.2 million fewer diluted shares from buybacks. Cash fell to $288.1M from $337.7M at fiscal year-start after $628.7M returned via buybacks and dividends; the board raised the quarterly dividend 5% to $1.16/share. No forward guidance appears in this filing.

drivers.explanation: Growth was driven by a 7.0% organic increase, partly offset by a 0.6-point drag from the prior-year disposition of a business; all three segments grew, led by the Americas from workstations and data solutions.
Rose 220bp of revenue, mainly from higher employee compensation tied to restructuring charges, plus increased cloud/technology spend and higher amortization from capitalized internal-use software.

Compression is explained by SG&A rising 430bp of revenue (higher variable and stock-based comp, one-time CEO make-whole pay, a forex-hedge settlement loss) plus cost of services rising 220bp, partly offset by revenue growth.
Decline was driven by higher operating expenses (employee compensation, restructuring/severance, CEO compensation costs) outpacing revenue growth.
Same operating-expense pressure as net income; the decline was partly offset by roughly 2.2 million fewer diluted shares outstanding from ongoing buybacks.

No forward guidance for next quarter or FY2026 appears in this filing. The board raised the quarterly dividend 5% to $1.16/share and continued buybacks ($628.7M returned over nine months), while flagging a continuing, unremediated IT-general-controls material weakness.
